sources.title: OpenStreetMap way/23672266 (replaced)
sources.note: ODbL. A single building outline covering both ruins, replaced on this map by two traced outlines. Edit dates are not construction dates.

sources.title: Naga City Ordinance No. 2003-003, Section 6
sources.note: Enacted January 15, 2003. Lists the two stone buildings at the old Post Office site on Peñafrancia Avenue.

sources.title: Dateline Ibalon: Spanish-era Buildings Declared as Important Cultural Properties in Naga City (July 2024)
sources.note: Places the 1826 inscription on the right building as seen from Peñafrancia Avenue, so this left (northeast) building is the jail. Cites the 1943 "Naga Jail, beside the post office building" and a historian's 1846 date for the jail's construction.

sources.title: Dateline Ibalon: The movement to protect Naga City's remaining cultural properties (February 2026)
sources.note: Reports a 20-day RTC Naga temporary restraining order of February 10, 2026 suspending construction in front of the ruins.

sources.title: Google Street View
sources.note: August 2025 panorama inspected October 8, 2026. From Peñafrancia Avenue, two roofless masonry ruins stand behind a fence: a long building with about seven arched, barred openings (left, northeast) and a smaller one (right, southwest). Capture dates are not construction dates. No image is saved or distributed.

sources.title: Outline traced from Google Maps satellite (z21)
sources.note: Inspected October 8, 2026. OSM maps both roofless ruins as one outline, way/23672266, which these two curated outlines replace. The long northeast ruin was traced from its walls on the satellite mosaic, then the traced pair was shifted (no rotation) so its centre matches the OSM outline. Accuracy is about two metres. Imagery date unknown; no bitmap ships.

text.en: The two stone buildings at the old Post Office site were listed for preservation by City Ordinance No. 2003-003.
Historian Danilo Gerona dates the construction of the provincial jail to 1846.
A 1943 account of the Japanese occupation records prisoners held in the Naga Jail, beside the post office building.
The city council declared the two Spanish-era buildings Important Cultural Properties through Resolution No. 2024-264, adopted May 7, 2024.
On February 10, 2026, the Naga RTC issued a 20-day restraining order suspending construction in front of the ruins.
